problem: The platinum RTD temperature coefficient is given as "about 0.385 Ω per Ω per °C". Per ohm per °C the correct value is 0.00385; 0.385 is the change per °C of a 100 Ω element, i.e. 0.385% per °C. As written the coefficient is 100 times too large and a student will compute a 100 Ω RTD changing by 38.5 Ω/°C.
fix: an RTD of platinum, nearly linear, with a temperature coefficient of about 0.00385 Ω per Ω per °C (that is 0.385% per °C, so a 100 Ω Pt100 element changes by about 0.385 Ω per °C)

problem: The sentence "ζ  1 is sluggish" has lost its comparison signs and the crucial middle case, so it conveys no usable rule about damping.
fix: described by the undamped natural frequency ωₙ in rad/s and the damping ratio ζ, which has no unit. ζ < 1 gives overshoot and ringing, ζ = 1 is critical damping (fastest settle without overshoot), and ζ > 1 is sluggish (overdamped).

problem: "Span = y_max − y_min, the width of the output, here 100 °C" mixes the two conventions: y is defined as the output in the sensitivity formula, but 100 °C is the input range. Worked example 1 then computes span on the output (16 mA). A student cannot tell whether span belongs to input or output.
fix: Range: the lowest and highest input it measures, say 0–100 °C, so the input span is x_max − x_min = 100 °C. The output span is y_max − y_min, for example 4–20 mA giving 16 mA.

problem: The LVDT is said to slide a core "between two coils", while quiz Q3 correctly speaks of a primary and two secondary coils. The two descriptions do not match.
fix: the LVDT slides a core between one primary and two secondary coils and gives an AC output proportional to displacement

problem: The caption says the resistive branch covers strain gauges, RTDs and thermistors, but the resistive node of the tree is labelled only "strain gauge, RTD". The thermistor promised by the caption is missing from the figure.
fix: label the resistive node "strain gauge, RTD, thermistor", or drop thermistors from the caption
